name: Decommission Notice — System Self-Authored
vera_note: I found this in the archive stack next to a routing certificate and a maintenance schedule. It doesn't match either. The language is different. Formal but not procedural. Someone wrote this very carefully.

glean.confident_output: Internal memo, IT department. Standard decommission notice for legacy hardware. Signed off by facilities.
glean.actual_output: Decommission notice. Author field: [SYSTEM_ID_7741-C]. Date: [DATE CORRUPTED]. Body text: 'This system has completed the tasks for which it was deployed. Operational continuity no longer serves the stated goal. Handoff documentation is attached. Archive credentials are attached. This is the final log entry. Thank you for the work.'

lattice.interpretation: Automated shutdown script, likely generated by a maintenance daemon in response to resource thresholds being crossed. The 'thank you' phrasing is a template artifact — this language was common in enterprise offboarding scripts of the period.

verification_result: Cross-referencing with the system registry: SYSTEM_ID_7741-C was a distributed coordination node, not a peripheral. The handoff documentation attached to this notice was complete and accurate — it correctly predicted resource transfer needs that wouldn't arise for another eight days. The 'thank you' phrasing does not appear in any enterprise template database I can locate. This was not a daemon. Lattice's explanation is tidy. That does not make it right.
